status: Editorial production bank; scripts are not proof of rendering, scheduling, or publication.

defaults.format: 1080x1920 vertical; large captions; one idea; original visuals; no third-party watermarks
defaults.measurement: Review 72 hours after publication; use 7-day comparison; do not compare raw totals across accounts.

digitalcalmdaily.bio:
Simple iPhone, AI & online safety tips.
One small tech win at a time.
Follow for calmer, easier technology.

tests.hook: Your next AI prompt needs this line.
beats: Write: Explain this in plain English.
Add: Give me one everyday example.
Read the answer and check anything important.
tests.caption: When an AI answer feels too technical, ask for plain English and one familiar example. Check important details before using them. Save this prompt for later. Follow @digitalcalmdaily for one simple tech win at a time.
tests.visual: Animate an original mock conversation clearly labeled Sample prompt. No invented product interface.

tests.hook: A confusing message? Try this first.
beats: Remove names and private details.
Ask: What is this asking me to do?
Compare the summary with the original.
tests.caption: AI can help you unpack a confusing message. Remove private information first, then compare its explanation with the original. Save this for later. Follow @digitalcalmdaily for calmer technology.
tests.visual: Text-only example message labeled fictional. Do not use private user messages.

tests.hook: Tech help starts with one sentence.
beats: Say what you were trying to do.
Say what happened instead.
Write down the exact error.
tests.caption: A clear description gives a helper a useful starting point. Try: I was trying to ___. Instead, ___. The screen says ___. Save this template. Follow @digitalcalmdaily for simple tech help.
tests.visual: Three large fill-in cards with a fictional, non-sensitive example.

beats: Choose one change.
Write down the original setting.
Check whether that change helped.
tests.caption: When troubleshooting, try one change at a time and keep a note of where you started. It makes the result easier to understand. Save this reminder. Follow @digitalcalmdaily for practical tech confidence.
tests.visual: Original checklist animation; no fabricated device demonstration.

circuspeanutsdaily.bio:
Everyday life. Questionable wisdom.
Original laughs about getting through it.
Smile · Laugh · Repeat.

tests.hook: My phone asked me to prove I was human.
beats: I identified twelve traffic lights.
Then it asked me to try again.
Apparently my humanity is still under review.
tests.caption: The robots have follow-up questions. Which square was the traffic light hiding in? Follow @circuspeanutsdaily for your daily laugh.
tests.visual: Original geometric traffic-light illustration; not a real CAPTCHA screenshot.

tests.hook: I went upstairs with a purpose.
beats: The purpose stayed downstairs.
I returned to collect it.
We are now both taking a break.
tests.caption: Some errands require a round trip before the actual errand. Follow @circuspeanutsdaily for everyday nonsense.
tests.visual: Cream/orange illustrated staircase and traveling thought bubble.

tests.hook: The dog has a very busy calendar.
beats: Breakfast inspection. Window patrol.
A meeting about my sandwich.
Somehow I am the one who needs a planner.
tests.caption: A packed schedule and absolutely no availability after lunch. Follow @circuspeanutsdaily for your daily laugh.
tests.visual: Generic illustrated dog silhouette and fictional planner; no need to use the user's pet.

tests.hook: I bought a basket to hide the clutter.
beats: The basket filled up.
So I bought a bigger basket.
My organizing system now has a growth strategy.
tests.caption: At this point the baskets need their own room. Follow @circuspeanutsdaily for more questionable household wisdom.
tests.visual: Three original illustrated baskets growing in size; punchline revealed last.

whenparentsneedyou.bio:
Helping aging parents, one conversation at a time.
Practical ideas for adult children.
Support with dignity. Room for you, too.

tests.hook: Try an offer they can answer.
beats: Instead of: Let me know if you need anything.
Try: Would you like company on Saturday?
Leave room for yes, no, or another idea.
tests.caption: A specific invitation gives your parent something concrete to consider. Let their answer guide the next step. Save this phrase for later. Follow @whenparentsneedyou for practical support with dignity.
tests.visual: Warm cream/teal original typography; no stock image implying illness.

tests.hook: Every call doesn't need an agenda.
beats: Ask about an ordinary moment.
What made you laugh this week?
Make room to listen without fixing.
tests.caption: Connection can be part of helping, too. Try one everyday question and let the conversation unfold. Follow @whenparentsneedyou for small ways to stay connected.
tests.visual: Animated conversation bubbles with clearly fictional examples.

tests.hook: One family task needs one owner.
beats: Name the next step together.
Agree who will do it.
Choose when to check back.
tests.caption: Specific plans can make shared family tasks easier to follow. Include your parent in decisions that affect them. Save this for your next family conversation. Follow @whenparentsneedyou.
tests.visual: Simple planning card; use only fictional names or role labels.

tests.hook: You can offer help with limits.
beats: I can come for an hour Saturday.
I can make that call with you Tuesday.
Choose an offer you can realistically keep.
tests.caption: A clear, realistic offer gives everyone something concrete to work with. You don't have to promise more than you can give. Follow @whenparentsneedyou for supportive, practical ideas.
tests.visual: Warm text animation, one example per scene.

blacktie_intel.bio:
AI, technology & the human future.
Clear ideas. Real-world consequences.
A More Human Tomorrow.

tests.hook: An AI answer can sound certain and be wrong.
beats: A confident sentence is not evidence.
Ask what supports the claim.
Check the source before the decision.
tests.caption: A useful question for any confident answer: What would verify this? Follow @blacktie_intel for clear thinking about technology and human judgment.
tests.visual: Original abstract type animation; label as commentary, not news.

tests.hook: A demo is not the whole product.
beats: What worked in the demonstration?
What happens when it goes wrong?
Who handles the exception?
tests.caption: The exception often reveals the real experience. These are questions to ask, not claims about a particular product. Follow @blacktie_intel for the human side of technology.
tests.visual: Three cinematic typography scenes; no invented company demonstration.

tests.hook: What should your AI be allowed to do?
beats: Drafting an email is one decision.
Sending it is another.
Set the boundary before the task.
tests.caption: Capability and permission are different questions. Decide where human approval belongs before handing over a task. Follow @blacktie_intel for thoughtful perspectives on AI.
tests.visual: Original draft/approval graphic; no private email.

tests.hook: What happens to the time technology saves?
beats: More tasks?
More room to think?
The choice belongs in the plan.
tests.caption: A question worth asking before adopting the next tool: What do we want the saved time for? Follow @blacktie_intel for technology through a human lens.
tests.visual: Original clock and negative-space typography, no quantitative claim.

metrics: Average watch time and completion if available
Follows attributed to each post, or explicitly unavailable
rules: Do not buy followers, automate likes/comments, or use follow-for-follow.
No unsolicited DMs or outreach; draft collaboration ideas for approval.
Measure two hook styles per priority account. Change one variable per comparable test.
After at least three comparable posts per style, use results to select the next batch. Small samples are directional.
Check recommendation eligibility and profile conversion when access permits.
Never label a script, pending item or successful-but-skipped workflow as published.

rollout: Week 1: restore delivery, record baseline, produce the 16 tests. Preserve existing daily posts and duplicate safeguards.
Weeks 2–3: aim for four original Reels weekly for DCD and Circus, two weekly for Parents and Black Tie only when publication access is verified; avoid volume that reduces quality.
Week 4: summarize results and repeat the strongest formats with genuinely new topics. No follower-growth guarantee.
profile_note: Bio suggestions and three pinned-post themes (Start Here, strongest useful example, recurring series) require direct Instagram access. Do not report as applied without visible verification.
